text: The Patriots continue their roster shuffling and injury management ahead of Sunday's trip to Buffalo, signing offensive lineman Matt Pryor from Arizona's practice squad even as they placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve with a thigh injury—a move that further tests the offensive line infrastructure around Drake Maye just as the quarterback insists his right shoulder is fine and ready to perform. Maye, who acknowledged Wednesday that better decision-making rather than physical limitations will be key to reversing the team's 1-2 start, faces a Bills offense led by Josh Allen, who has proven capable of shaking off sloppy performances and coming back strong. The Patriots rank dead last in offensive points per game at 9.7, making this Week 4 AFC East showdown against the undefeated Bills at Highmark Stadium not just an opportunity for New England to salvage early momentum, but a chance to diagnose whether the offensive struggles stem from Maye's judgment or the supporting cast around him. Meanwhile, Ann Maye, the quarterback's wife, has been active in the community this week, presenting a $100,000 donation from the MayeDay Family Foundation to Family Food Connections to support families facing food insecurity.
